examples.question_text: The probability that a parcel arrives on time is $\frac{11}{15}$. Find the probability that it does not arrive on time.
examples.solution_text:
Let $A$ be the event that the parcel arrives on time. Its complement is arriving late.

$\begin{aligned}P(A')&=1-P(A)\\&=1-\frac{11}{15}\\&=\frac{4}{15}\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text:
One card is selected at random from $40$ cards numbered $1$ to $40$. Let $A$ be the event that its number is even and $B$ the event that its number is less than $13$.

(a) Use the addition rule to find $P(A\cup B)$.

(b) Hence find the probability that neither event occurs.

A bag contains $5$ red, $4$ green, $3$ blue and $8$ yellow counters. One counter is selected at random.

(a) Find the probability that it is red, green or blue.

(b) Hence find the probability that it is yellow.

Two events satisfy $P(A)=0.48$, $P(B)=0.37$ and $P(A\cup B)=0.70$.

(a) Find $P(A\cap B)$.

(b) Find $P(A'\cap B)$.

At a service, the probability that a machine needs an oil change is $\frac{7}{10}$, and the probability that it needs both an oil change and a filter change is $\frac{1}{5}$. Find the probability that it needs an oil change without a filter change.
Two events have $P(A)=\frac{m}{m+n}$, $P(B)=\frac{n}{m+n}$ and $P(A\cap B)=\frac{1}{m+n}$, where $m,n$ are positive integers and $m+n=30$. If $P(A\cap B')=0.40$, find $m$ and $n$.
Events $A$ and $B$ satisfy $P(A)=\frac{3}{5}$, $P(B)=\frac{1}{2}$ and $P(A\cap B)=\frac{3}{10}$. Find $P(A'\cup B')$, the probability that at least one event does not occur.

examples.derivation: There are 20 even cards, 12 cards below 13 and 6 in both groups. The union contains 20 + 12 − 6 = 26 cards, giving 13/20. Neither contains 14 cards, giving 7/20. Diagram regions 14, 6, 6 and 14 agree.
The 20 counters belong to disjoint colour categories. Red, green or blue has probability (5 + 4 + 3)/20 = 3/5; yellow has probability 1 − 3/5 = 2/5. The diagram represents all counts correctly.
The intersection is 0.48 + 0.37 − 0.70 = 0.15. B only is 0.37 − 0.15 = 0.22. A only is 0.33 and neither is 0.30; all four diagram regions sum to 1.

Oil change without filter change has probability 7/10 − 1/5 = 1/2. The clipping and white mask shade O only, excluding the overlap. Labels show the derived exclusive probability and given intersection without inventing unspecified regions.
A only has probability (m − 1)/30 = 0.40, so m − 1 = 12, m = 13 and n = 17. Diagram regions become 12/30, 1/30, 16/30 and 1/30, summing to 1 and reproducing both marginal probabilities.

At least one event not occurring is the complement of both occurring, so its probability is 1 − 3/10 = 7/10. A only is 3/10, B only is 1/5 and neither is 1/5. The diagram shades these three regions and leaves only the intersection white.
